Order On Board 01.10.2024
1.

This appeal has been filed under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short the "Act 1894") challenging the award dated 13.07.2011 passed by the Additional District Judge, Janjgir in MJC No.25-A/2010, whereby reference application preferred by the appellant under Section 18 (2)
of the Act 1894 seeking enhancement of award amount passed by the Land Acquisition Officer (Revenue), Janjgir-Champa on 29.03.2008, has been dismissed.
Maniram Jagat vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99539315/
1 2.

entities.text: Maniram Jagat vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant was the owner of acquired land admeasuring area 3.72 acres situated at Village Parsahinala, Patwari Halka No.3, Tahsil Akalatara, Janjgir-Champa.

The said lands were acquired by the respondent/State for construction of Karrnala Dam for which compensation has been determined to the tune of Rs.3,53,055/- in Land Acquisition Case No.05/A-82/2006-07.

Out of the aforesaid lands, the calculation has been made in respect of two lands bearing Khasra No.319/5 area 0.02 acre and Khara No.336/2 area 0.07 acre as irrigated land and compensation has made at the rate of Rs.1,11,966/- per acre, however, compensation in respect of other lands have been calculated as non-irrigated land at the rate of Rs.68,217/- per acre.
The detailed calculation in this regard is mentioned at Sr. No.97 of Form-13 attached with award dated 29.03.2008 issued by SDO (Revenue), Janjgir.
Thereby, total compensation of Rs.3,53,055/- has been paid to the appellant by way of cheque.

3. The appellant being dissatisfied by the assessment of compensation and for treating his land to be non-irrigated, filed the reference application under Section 18 of the Act 1894 before the Collector,
Janjgir-Champa for proper assessment of the land on the ground that his land was irrigated and double cropped.
4. The Collector after considering the said application referred the matter to the Court of Additional District Judge, Janjgir vide memo dated 12.03.2010.

entities.text: Court of Additional District Judge, Janjgir
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned trial Court has framed and considered five issues while passing the impugned award.
The appellant in order to prove his case examined himself and one witness namely Nathuram (AW-2) and exhibited 3 documents A-1, A-2 and A-3.
The non-applicants have examined S. L. Yadav (NAW-1), Sub Divisional Officer, Water Resource Department, Janjg-Champa.

After evaluating evidence on record, learned trial Court reached to the conclusion that neither any documentary evidence has been proved nor any witness has been examined to prove documents A-1 to A-3 produced by the appellant.
After considering the evidence of NAW-1 who has deposed that the said land is non-irrigated land, dismissed the reference by the impugned award.
Hence, this petition.

5. It is pertinent to mention here that this appeal has been preferred in the year 2011 and after lapse of substantial period, on 31.08.2018, the appellant has filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC (IA No.1/2018) for taking additional documents on record.
The said document is copy of Khasra Panchshala pertaining to the year 2004-05 and 2007-08.
It is stated in the application that said documents were received on 20.08.2018 and thereafter the same has been filed.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that findings recorded by the trial Court are perverse to the evidence on record.

He submits that during trial the appellant has produced the documents related to irrigation i.e. A-1 to A-3 which have been issued by the concerned Irrigation Department to prove the fact that the acquired land is irrigated land, however, the trial Court has not appreciated the evidence in proper perspective.

Learned counsel further submits that by way of application under Order 47 Rule 11 CPC the appellant wants to show that for two lands i.e. Khasra No.319/5 &
336/2 the compensation was awarded on the basis of irrigation land but in Khasra entries for such lands nothing has been mentioned about irrigated land and only remark was made that appellant is taking paddy crop for the concerned Khasra entries for the year 2004-05 & 2007-08.

Therefore, the said documents are necessary to advance the cause of justice, therefore, the same may be Maniram Jagat vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99539315/
2 considered.

entities.text: Maniram Jagat vs State Of Chhattisgarh And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of such submission, he prays to allow this appeal and enhance compensation on the basis of irrigated land.

7. On the contrary, learned counsel for the State opposes the aforesaid submission and refers to the statement of S.L. Yadav, SDO of Water Resource Department (NAW-1), who has stated that at the time of acquisition, the subject land was non-irrigated land.
He further submits that neither the appellant has proved any documentary evidence filed by him nor produced any document to show that subject land was irrigated land.
He submits that oral statement of the appellant and his witness is not sufficient to establish the fact that such land is double cropped.
He further submits that in the application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC the appellant has not assigned proper and sufficient reasons as per three conditions stipulated under the provisions of CPC.
Therefore, such documents may not be accepted at a belated stage.
He also submits that even if such documents are taken on record, such documents would be of no help to the petitioner as there is no mention about double crop in column No.7.
Hence, findings arrived at the trial Court is just and proper and does not call for any interference by this Court.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

Maniram Jagat (AW-1) in his evidence has categorically admitted the fact that the land which is irrigated or the land on which there is plants and trees, entry of such land is endorsed by the Patwari in Khasra records.
Nathuram (AW-2) in his evidence admitted that he is not aware about the fact that whether the entries of irrigated land is made by the Patwari.
10. Perusal of overall record would show that the appellant has not produced any document to prove the fact that the subject land was irrigated land.

The documents produced by the appellant i.e. A-1 to A-3 relates to irrigation slip provided by the Water Resource Department which have also not been proved by any of the witnesses of the concerned Department.

Further, though the document relating to Khasra Panchshala have been filed by the appellant by application under Order 41 Rule 27,
however, the appellant has not assigned sufficient reasons as to why such documents could not be filed before the reference/trial Court.
Even no entry has been made with regard to subject land for which reference was made to treat it as irrigated land or double cropped.

Moreover, determination and assessment of compensation for two parts of the land i.e. Khasra Nos.319/5 and 336/2 was made by the Acquisition Authority on the basis of criteria and conditions made for irrigated land and since other lands have not fulfilled such criteria during scrutiny, compensation has been made by treating it to be non-irrigated land.

11. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Court reaches to the conclusion that the appellant has failed to produce any reliable piece of evidence to prove the subject land to be irrigated one and hence no case is made out for enhancement of compensation.
12.
The findings recorded by the reference/trial Court is just and proper and same do not call for any interference by this Court.
